minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 18, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor MacLean at
5:05 p.m., on January 18, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 13, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:39 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor MacLean

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

RECESS

City Council Minutes  1  January 18, 2010
 At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor MacLean declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize the Saddleback Valley Wolverines, Jr. Midget Football Team for
  Winning the Pop Warner Western Conference Championship and Placing Second
  in the Pop Warner National Championship in Florida

  Mayor MacLean presented certificates of commendation to the team members and
  coaches of the Saddleback Valley Wolverines.

P2.  Recognize Mission Viejo’s Community Recycling Program Award Winner

  Mayor MacLean and Michelle Clark, Waste Management, presented the award to
  Melissa Palencia, representing the Shops at Mission Viejo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: read from the back of the City Council Agenda cover sheet where the
Council Meeting rules for decorum are outlined. He stated that the Mayor should have called a
recess two weeks ago when the meeting was disrupted.

Mark Dobrilovic, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction with the way Mayor MacLean conducted the
last meeting and noted that he should not have been asked to leave the meeting.

David Allen, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo is the best city in America to live, to work, and to
raise a family. He expressed concern with the recall efforts and he urged all voters to get
involved and understand what their vote will mean.

Matt Corrigan, M.V.: read excerpts from a newspaper article describing an incident that Mayor
MacLean was involved in at his former workplace, UCI.

Barbara Anderson, M.V.: stated that Council Meetings are meant for business and not for
politicking.

Sharon Cody, M.V.: discussed alleged illegal actions of one of the recall proponents and
encouraged residents to vote no on the recall and for Dave Leckness in case the recall is
successful.

Helen Workun, M.V.: urged residents to vote on February 2nd, to vote no on the recall and for
Dave  Leckness  to  preserve  the  quality  of  life  in  Mission  Viejo.
Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: expressed concern that an email she sent to a number of her friends was
copied by another resident, reworded to make it look like she was in favor of the recall, and then
the email was re-sent to her friends.

City Council Minutes  2  January 18, 2010
 Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that the negativity brought about by the recall effort is not
healthy for Mission Viejo and she encouraged residents to vote no on the recall.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes from the regular City Council Meeting of January 4, 2010, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register dated December 4, 2009, in the amount of $1,503,913.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated December 11, 2009, in the amount of $609,183.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated December 18, 2009, in the amount of $1,228,908.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register dated December 25, 2009, in the amount of $1,244,131.75

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for November 2009

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  January 18, 2010
 8.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for November 2009

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer's Monthly Report for November 2009

  Received and filed.

10.  Ethernet Switch Purchase for Fiber Communications and Traffic Controller
  Update Project-Various Locations (CIP 797)

  Approved purchase agreement in the amount of $238,093.00 with Resilient
  Communications for ethernet switches.

11.  Claim Against the City - Sherry Little

  Rejected the claim.

PUBLIC HEARING

12.  Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2009-218 filed by Gil Gonzalez of
  Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T Wireless, of the Planning and
  Transportation Commission’s November 9, 2009, denial of a petition submitted by
  AT&T Wireless to construct a wireless telecommunication facility at Florence-
  Joyner Olympiad Park, 22761 Olympiad Road, in the R (Recreation) zone.

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Christian Murdock, Assistant Planner, presented a visual representation of the proposed
  cell tower via photographs and an architectural site plan.

  All City Council Members noted that they have visited the site either recently or in the
  past.

  At the hour of 6:54 p.m., Mayor MacLean opened the public hearing.

  Gil Gonzalez, Trillium Consulting, Inc., agent for AT&T Wireless: outlined the proposed
  wireless telecommunication facility and presented a dropped call data sheet which
  indicates that there is an average of 150 to 200 calls per day. Mr. Gonzalez stated that
  they are trying to provide seamless cell coverage in that area.

RECESS

City Council Minutes  4  January 18, 2010
 At the hour of 7:06 p.m., Mayor MacLean declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
7:19 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

  Gil Gonzalez provided answers to questions that were posed by the City Council
  Members.

  The following spoke in opposition to the proposed wireless facility: Larry Gilbert, M.V.
  and Stephanie Tanton, M.V.

  Gil Gonzalez provided rebuttal comments in response to points that were made by the
  public speakers.

  At  the  hour  of  7:36  p.m.,  Mayor  MacLean  closed  the  public  hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 10-03 Denying the Appeal Petition, and Thereby Denying PDP2009-218.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

13.  Outdoor Fitness Equipment for Senior Citizens and Public Use at Oso Viejo Park

  City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the installation of outdoor fitness equipment at Oso
  Viejo Park: Anna T. Boyce M.V. and Helen Workun, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to
  approve the concept, direct staff to conduct normal community outreach and return to the
  City Council for authorization to go out to bid for installation of the equipment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  5  January 18, 2010
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

15.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

16.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

17.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

In light of the current rain storm, City Manager Wilberg reminded residents that the City
furnishes sandbags and distribution locations can be found by visiting the City blog at
http://missionviejolife.org/ or the web site, http://www.cityofmissionviejo.org/.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Reminded residents to stock up on batteries and flash lights because power outages can occur in
the storms that are forecasted this week.

City Council Minutes  6  January 18, 2010
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht discussed the devastation and loss of life in Haiti and stated that the
tragedy there should remind us to be prepared for our own emergencies and to be self-reliant.
She reiterated that the City is currently making sandbags available to residents in need. Council
Member Schlicht stated that our citizens are our legacy and we are thankful that all of the
missionaries from Mission Viejo Christian Church have returned home safely and we are
bursting with pride that Diablos Quarterback Mark Sanchez led the New York Jets to victory
yesterday. She noted that these people are just some of the “doers” of our community. She also
reminded residents that as Americans, we celebrate Martin Luther King Day to honor the
peaceful protester. Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that Cox Communications
extended her a last minute invitation to attend their recall forum and she asked how Council
Member Ury can address the allegations of Lance MacLean’s violence if he wasn’t present at the
UCI incident nor was he present at the altercation with resident and Council Candidate Diane
Greenwood. She stated that anything Frank Ury says about Lance MacLean’s behavior is
nothing but third party hearsay, yet the OC Weekly recently reported excerpts from the police
report in the UCI event and she read from that article. She stated that she was shocked that Cox
did not hold a candidate forum for the recall election when they have provided that service for
over fifteen years and she hopes that the City Clerk will follow-up and see if the Cox Infomercial
is reported on Mr. MacLean’s campaign filings.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury thanked Cox Communications for providing the forum regarding the
upcoming recall election. He stated that he knows, for a fact, that the invitations went out to all
interested parties yet just a few hours before the taping a supporter of the recall, who had
previously committed, declined to attend. He stated that if Lance MacLean wasn’t invited to the
forum he certainly couldn’t be Lance’s surrogate. What he did was spend some time discussing
why the expenditure of $270,000, several months before a general election, is not a good use of
taxpayer dollars. He stated that the democratic process can get hindered and while many people
have asked him if there is anything the City can do about the election, he observed that we are
required to spend the money and therefore he encourages residents to get out and vote.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stood by her previous comments regarding events at the last Council
Meeting. She stated that she was very disturbed that members of the audience were calling out
and heckling while the public speakers were trying to give their address. She noted that people
have told her they don’t want to speak at Council meetings because they are afraid, and one of
her friends reported that they received a phone call after they spoke at a meeting. She stated that
this has to be a safe place for anyone to speak and no one should be subjected to rudeness,
smirks, or heckling. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked all of those who attended the blood drive
that she organized in honor of Hometown Hero, Marine Alex Minsky. She stated that it is
important for us to remember our men and women in uniform and she is happy to report that Mr.

City Council Minutes  7  January 18, 2010
 Minsky is doing much better now. She also outlined her attended at the Elk’s annual
appreciation dinner to honor law enforcement and firefighters of the year. She was proud to be
there and recognize Mission Viejo Deputy Brad Kenneally, Firefighter Captain Jack Perisho and
Reserve Firefighter Kevin Gates. She thanked the Elks for this annual dinner to honor those who
keep us safe. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley acknowledged the team of missionaries from Mission
Viejo Christian Church and Grace Community Church who were in Haiti helping at an
orphanage when the earthquake struck. They were able to minister to the needs of those who
were injured in the earthquake and none of the missionaries were hurt. She noted that all of the
missionaries have come home safely but one, Robert Taylor, wanted to stay and continue to help.
Mayor Pro tem Kelley asked residents to remember the people of Haiti and our resident, Robert
Taylor in their thoughts and prayers.

Mayor MacLean

Mayor MacLean stated that there continue to be a number of allegations thrown his way and they
are intended to impugn his character. He addressed the incident at UCI and stated that in
hindsight, it should have been handled in a different way but he hopes that no one is ever put in a
position where they fear for the safety of others and have to make a snap decision. Looking
back, he feels that he handled the situation inappropriately and he has paid a dear price for that.
He feels he has learned a very valuable lesson and he is a better person for it. He noted that
Martin Luther King was an example of someone who moved things forward through the use of
civil discourse. Mayor MacLean compared those qualities to the traits displayed at the last
meeting and he stated that he asked Deputy Sandberg to remove a member of the audience
because he was being boisterous and disruptive. He also expressed concern over a recent
incident on a Mission Viejo street corner when his supporters were harassed by proponents of the
recall. He stated that the recall proponents made catcalls and tried to intimidate his supporters
and therefore he asks people to step back, allow others to exercise their first amendment rights,
and express their opinions. He also announced that he will place an item on an upcoming agenda
and will ask his colleagues to sign a voluntary Code of Civility which will mean that they agree
to conduct business in a respectful and courteous manner, even in the face of disagreement.
Mayor MacLean concluded his comments by wishing residents safety during the rain storms.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:21 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor MacLean adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 1, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 1, 2010

City Council Minutes  8  January 18, 2010
